questions.q: A patient with hypocalcaemia has an appropriate rise in parathyroid hormone. Which renal effect contributes to restoration of plasma calcium?
options: Increased calcium reabsorption in the distal nephron
questions.explain: Parathyroid hormone increases renal calcium reabsorption, especially in the distal nephron, while reducing proximal phosphate reabsorption. It also stimulates renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase, increasing calcitriol production.

questions.q: A child with untreated congenital hypothyroidism has impaired growth and neurodevelopment. Which thyroid hormone action is especially important for normal early brain development?
options: Promotion of neuronal differentiation and maturation
questions.explain: Thyroid hormone is essential for normal brain development, including neuronal differentiation, synapse formation and myelination. Severe deficiency during early life can cause permanent neurodevelopmental impairment if not treated promptly.

questions.q: Which cell type secretes calcitonin in response to elevated plasma calcium?
questions.explain: Thyroid parafollicular C cells release calcitonin when plasma calcium rises. Its role in normal adult calcium homeostasis is relatively modest compared with PTH and vitamin D.

questions.q: Which enzyme in the proximal renal tubule converts 25-hydroxyvitamin D to active 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D?
questions.explain: Renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase converts 25-hydroxyvitamin D to calcitriol. Its activity is stimulated by PTH and regulated by phosphate and FGF23.

questions.q: Which thyroid hormone is secreted in the greatest quantity by the thyroid gland and is converted in peripheral tissues to the more biologically active T3?
questions.explain: The thyroid secretes predominantly thyroxine (T4). Peripheral deiodinases convert T4 to T3, which has greater activity at thyroid hormone receptors.
